home.meta.title: Pot: group chat money that follows its own rules

home.hero.title: Group chat money that follows its own rules.

home.problem.title: Every group trip has a money problem
home.problem.front.title: One friend fronts it all
home.problem.front.body: Then they spend weeks chasing everyone to pay up.
home.problem.front.chat.label: Maya's group chat. She asks Leo for his $150 on day 2 and again on day 23. Leo is still typing.
home.problem.front.punchline: Leo has been typing since day 2.
home.problem.split.title: Split apps just keep score
home.problem.split.body: They track who owes what, but hold no money, so no one can pay from the group.
home.problem.shared.title: Shared accounts trust one person
home.problem.shared.body: The money sits in one person's name, and everyone else hopes for the best.
home.problem.pivot: What if the money lived right in the group chat?
home.how.title: Set the rules once. Then enjoy the trip.
home.how.create.title: Start a Pot and pick the rules
home.how.create.body: Name it for the trip and set its rules. They read like sentences, and the Pot enforces them itself.
home.how.share.title: Drop the link in the chat
home.how.share.body: Friends see the Pot before they sign in, join with Google and chip in their share.
home.how.instant.title: Small spends approve themselves
home.how.instant.body: Maya's $84 for groceries is under the $100 instant limit, so Pot rules approve it and send her the money in seconds.
home.how.group.title: Bigger spends need the group's OK
home.how.group.body: The $300 boat trip needs one OK from Sam or Leo. Leo taps OK, and it's on its way.
home.how.close.title: Close it and everyone gets their share back
home.how.close.body: When the trip's over, what's left is split by what each person put in. Maya, Sam and Leo get back $22 each.
home.trust.title: No one can take money out alone.
home.trust.body: Small spends follow the Pot's rules; bigger ones need the group.
home.trust.google.title: Sign in with Google
home.trust.google.body: No new password, and nothing to write down or lose.
home.trust.install.title: Nothing to install
home.trust.install.body: Pot opens from the link, in the browser you already use. Add it to your Home Screen if you like.
home.trust.back.title: Everyone gets their share back
home.trust.back.body: When the Pot closes, what's left is split by what each person put in. No spreadsheet needed.
home.tech.title: How NEAR makes it work
home.tech.intro: Pot keeps the jargon off the screen. Here's what runs underneath, on NEAR testnet today with test USDC.
home.tech.parts.label: Each part, up close
home.tech.auth.title: Zero NEAR, zero popups
home.tech.auth.hook: Sign in with Google. Then just tap.
home.tech.auth.scene: Maya continues with Google and she's in: her account holds 0 NEAR, and its key is saved on her phone, so there are no popups after that.
home.tech.relayer.title: Gas and deposits are on us
home.tech.relayer.hook: Taps are free. We pick up the bill.
home.tech.relayer.scene: What a tap costs you drops to $0.00: Pot pays the gas and the deposits.
home.tech.hub.title: A rulebot on a short leash
home.tech.hub.hook: It approves what the rules allow. Only.
home.tech.hub.scene: The rulebot lets spends up to $100 through: $84 for groceries is approved at once. $300 for a boat is over it, so it waits for one OK from anyone else in the group.
home.tech.majority.title: Majority rules. Literally.
home.tech.majority.hook: Bigger calls wait for most of the group.
home.tech.majority.scene: Closing the Pot: Maya and Sam approve, 2 of 3 members, a majority, so it's approved. Leo hasn't answered yet.
home.tech.dao.title: One Pot, one DAO, no keys
home.tech.dao.hook: It holds the money. Nobody holds a key.
home.tech.dao.tags: Sputnik DAO v2 · global contract · 0 keys
home.tech.dao.scene: A key can't get into {pot}: it has 0 keys. Only its seats can act: Maya, Sam, Leo and the rulebot.
home.tech.money.title: Dollars in, fair shares out
home.tech.money.hook: Close it: everyone gets their share back.
home.tech.money.scene: Maya, Sam and Leo each put in $150, $450 in all. Spends leave $66, and closing sends $22 back to each of them.
home.tech.demo.body: Follow the $84 grocery spend through a simulation: what Maya taps, what her phone signs, what our relayer sends, and how the Pot's Sputnik DAO approves it. Nothing is sent.
home.tech.demo.cta: See how it works, step by step

home.tech.flow.relay.title: Our relayer pays the gas

home.tech.flow.hub.body: It holds the 1-of-1 rulebot seat in every Pot.

home.final.body: Set it up, drop the link in the chat, and let the rules do the chasing.

demo.note.no_keys: The Pot's account has no access keys. Nobody can sign for it, not even us. It can only do what its members and the Hub's seat approve.
demo.note.status_lies: On NEAR a transaction can report success while a step inside it failed. Pot's relayer reads every receipt, here the last one: "150000000" used means the money was added.
demo.note.limits_in_hub: Sputnik itself enforces no limit: the Hub's seat could approve any transfer. The limits live in the Hub's code, which only votes on requests it filed a moment earlier. The Hub's own key is deleted at the planned lock, after which nobody can change that code. Until then, the README's Limitations say so.
demo.note.exact_kind: A vote carries a copy of the exact request. The DAO refuses it if the copy differs, so nobody approves something other than what they saw.
demo.note.payout_separate: Approving doesn't prove the money arrived: the payout is a separate receipt. Pot checks it, and sync records a failure if there is one.
demo.note.sync: Anyone may call sync. Our relayer does it after every vote, so the Hub's records always match the Pot.
demo.note.atomic: All three refunds run inside one receipt. If any one failed, all would be undone and the group could try again.
demo.note.busy: A close can't start within a minute of money moving, so a refund is never computed from a balance that's about to change.
demo.note.after_close: The $22 now sits in each person's Pot account. Pot has no cash-out yet; this is test money on testnet.
demo.glossary.title: Words in this chapter
demo.g.dao: A shared account run by rules instead of a person. Here every Pot is one, and its members approve what it does.
demo.g.sputnik_dao: NEAR's standard DAO contract. Pot uses its official code, installed by hash, unchanged.
demo.g.proposal: A request filed in the DAO, like “pay Maya $84” or “add Leo”. It runs only once enough seats approve it.
demo.g.role: A named group in the DAO with its own powers. A Pot has two: member (the friends) and rulebot (only the Pot Hub).
demo.g.threshold: How many approvals a role needs. Members need a majority: 2 of 3 here.
demo.g.quorum: The minimum number of approvals ever accepted. Pot sets it to 1, so nothing can pass with zero votes.
demo.g.rulebot: The Pot Hub's seat in every Pot. One vote from it approves transfers and new members, and the Hub only casts it when the Pot's rules allow.
demo.g.pot_hub: Pot's own contract (pots.potprev.testnet). It creates each Pot, checks the rules, holds the rulebot seat and keeps the ledger of who put in what.
demo.g.policy: The DAO's rulebook: its roles, their powers, thresholds and the 7-day voting period.
demo.g.delegate_action: A request the user signs but doesn't send (NEP-366). Someone else wraps it in a transaction and pays for it; contracts still see the user as the caller.
demo.g.relayer: Pot's server account (users.potprev.testnet) that sends signed requests and pays their gas, so users need 0 NEAR. It refuses anything outside an allowlist.
demo.g.transaction: What gets submitted to NEAR. Here the relayer signs it, and the user's request rides inside.
demo.g.receipt: One step of a transaction's work, run by one account. A transaction fans out into receipts as contracts call each other.
demo.g.callback: A receipt that runs after another finishes and reads its result.
demo.g.gas: The work a call may use, bought in NEAR. 1 Tgas is a trillion gas, about 0.0001 NEAR. Unused gas is refunded.
demo.g.yoctonear: The smallest unit of NEAR: 10⁻²⁴ NEAR. Token transfers must attach exactly 1, to prove a full-access key signed them.
demo.g.deposit: NEAR attached to a call. In Pot it is 0 everywhere except that 1 yoctoNEAR.
demo.g.storage_prepay: NEAR the Hub sends with each proposal, so the Pot can pay for the bytes it stores.
demo.g.nonce: A counter on each key. Every signature uses a higher one, so an old signature can't be replayed.
demo.g.max_block_height: The block after which a signed request expires: about 2 minutes here.
demo.g.device_key: The key Pot keeps on your phone (non-extractable). It signs your requests without a popup.
demo.g.ed25519: The kind of digital signature NEAR uses: 64 bytes that prove a key signed exactly this message.
demo.g.invite_key: A key made for one invite link. Its secret lives after the # in the link; the Hub stores only its public half.
demo.g.account: A NEAR account like u-3p8w2kdn.users.potprev.testnet. Pot creates it for you with 0 NEAR; your name lives off-chain.
demo.g.usdc: Pot's test dollar token on testnet (NEP-141, 6 decimals). It has no value.
demo.g.ft_transfer_call: Send tokens to a contract and call it in the same step. If the contract refuses, the tokens come back.
demo.g.global_contract: Contract code stored once on NEAR and used by many accounts by its hash. Every Pot uses Sputnik's this way, for 0.012 NEAR instead of 5.4.
demo.g.sync: A Hub method anyone can call to copy a proposal's final status from the Pot into the Hub's records.
demo.g.pro_rata: Split by what each person put in: everyone put in $150, so everyone gets an equal third.
demo.g.failure: The proposal stays approved but unpaid. Pot's relayer reads the payout receipt, records the failure with sync, and the request can be retried with Finalize. The demo shows only the happy path.
demo.c1.title: Maya starts a Pot
demo.c1.line: One tap creates the group's own account. No fee, no keys.
demo.c1.aha: Every Pot is [its own Sputnik DAO with no keys at all]. Its only seats are the members and the Pot Hub.
demo.c1.before: Maya signed in with Google earlier. Our relayer created her account u-7k2m9qxa.users.potprev.testnet with 0 NEAR and her phone's device key. She has no Pots yet.
demo.c1.b1: Maya names the Pot and picks a cover.
demo.c1.b2: She keeps the suggested rules: up to $100 without asking, $200 per person in total, bigger spends go to the group.
demo.c1.b3: Her phone signs one request: “Pot Hub, create Lisbon Trip for me.” No popup, no fee.
demo.c1.b4: This is all she [[delegate_action|signed]]. The [[pot_hub|Hub]] is the only contract it can reach.
demo.c1.b5: Our [[relayer|relayer]] puts her request in its own [[transaction|transaction]] and pays for it. Maya still has 0 NEAR.
demo.c1.b6: The Hub creates a new account for the Pot, gives it 0.05 NEAR to store its records, and installs the [[sputnik_dao|Sputnik DAO]] code with two seats: Maya, and the Hub.
demo.c1.b7: The Hub writes the Pot into its list and opens a [[usdc|USDC (test)]] balance for it, so it can hold dollars.
demo.c1.b8: Maya gets a link to drop in the group chat. The secret part after # never reaches a server.
demo.c2.title: Leo joins from the link
demo.c2.line: Two signatures on Leo's phone, and the Hub's seat lets him in.
demo.c2.aha: Joining is a DAO decision too, but a pre-approved one: [the Hub's single seat adds a member only when the invite signature checks out].
demo.c2.before: Leo tapped the link and signed in with Google. Our relayer created u-3p8w2kdn.users.potprev.testnet with 0 NEAR, added his device key and paid his USDC registration. The Pot has Maya and Sam, $300, and Sam's join (proposal #0) approved. Group approvals need 2 of 2.
demo.c2.b1: Leo sees who invited him, who's in, and the rules, before he commits to anything.
demo.c2.b2: Joining takes two signatures, both on Leo's phone.
demo.c2.b3: First, the secret in the link signs “Leo joins Lisbon Trip”. That proves he got the link, and it only works for Leo.
demo.c2.b4: Then his own key signs the request to the Hub, with that proof inside.
demo.c2.b5: The Hub checks the link is valid, then files a request in the Pot: “add Leo as a member”.
demo.c2.b6: The Hub approves it with its seat. For adding members it is the only vote needed, so Leo is in at once.
demo.c2.b7: Now three people can approve, and bigger spends need two of them.
demo.c2.b8: Leo is in, without ever paying a fee.
demo.c3.title: Leo adds his $150
demo.c3.line: The dollars pass through the Hub, which writes down who put in what.
demo.c3.aha: The money passes through the Hub and lands in the Pot in one chain of receipts. [The Hub writes down who put in what], which makes fair refunds possible later.
demo.c3.before: Leo has $150.00 of demo dollars, which the faucet (treasury.potprev.testnet) sent him off-screen. The Pot has $300.00 of $450.
demo.c3.b1: Leo adds his $150 share. The sheet shows the result before he taps.
demo.c3.b2: His phone signs one request, this time to the dollar token itself.
demo.c3.b3: He asks [[usdc|USDC]] to send $150 to the Pot Hub, with a note saying which Pot it's for.
demo.c3.b4: Token transfers need one [[yoctonear|yoctoNEAR]] attached, a millionth of a billionth of a billionth of a NEAR. The relayer pays even that.
demo.c3.b5: USDC moves the $150 to the Hub and tells it: “this came from Leo, for Lisbon Trip”.
demo.c3.b6: The Hub checks Leo is a member, passes the $150 on to the Pot, and writes down “Leo put in $150”.
demo.c3.b7: The Pot is full. Everyone's phone shows it.
demo.c4.title: $84 of groceries, approved by Pot rules
demo.c4.line: Nobody votes: the Hub's seat approves it, because the rules said yes.
demo.c4.aha: Nobody voted, yet the DAO approved it: [the Hub's seat approves only transfers it created because the rules said yes].
demo.c4.before: The Pot has $450.00. Maya has used $0 of her $200 without asking. Proposals #0 and #1 are approved joins.
demo.c4.b1: Maya paid $84 for groceries and wants it back. The sheet already says the rules allow it.
demo.c4.b2: Her phone signs one request to the Hub.
demo.c4.b3: She asks the Hub for $84 from Lisbon Trip, for groceries. She doesn't ask the group.
demo.c4.b4: The relayer sends it and pays. Maya: still 0 NEAR.
demo.c4.b5: The Hub checks the rules: $84 is under $100, Maya has $200 left, she's paying herself and she's a member who put money in. It also reads the Pot's real balance.
demo.c4.b6: Inside the rules, the Hub files a payout request in the Pot: $84 to Maya.
demo.c4.b7: The Hub approves with its [[rulebot|seat]]. That one vote is enough, because the rules said yes.
demo.c4.b8: The Pot itself sends Maya $84. The Hub reads the result back to be sure.
demo.c4.b9: About five seconds after her tap, the money is hers.
demo.c5.title: A $300 boat trip goes to the group
demo.c5.line: Over the limit, so two of the three friends approve it in the DAO itself.
demo.c5.aha: Above the one-OK limit the Hub can only file the request. [Two of the three friends must approve it in the DAO itself.]
demo.c5.before: The Pot has $366.00 and three members, so group approvals need 2 of 3.
demo.c5.b1: Maya wants $300 for the boat. That's over the limit, so the app says the group decides.
demo.c5.b2: She signs the same kind of request as for groceries.
demo.c5.b3: The Hub files it as proposal #3 and stops. It has no seat that can approve this.
demo.c5.b4: Her phone immediately adds her own approval. It sends the exact request she saw, so she can't approve something else by mistake.
demo.c5.b5: One more approval is needed. Leo and Sam get a notification.
demo.c5.b6: Now you're Leo. He reads what he'd approve: $300 to Maya, for tickets.
demo.c5.b7: Leo signs one vote, sent straight to the Pot, not to the Hub.
demo.c5.b8: That's the second of two. The Pot pays Maya $300 in the same moment.
demo.c5.b9: Our relayer then tells the Hub what happened, so its records match the Pot.
demo.c6.title: Close the Pot: $22 back each
demo.c6.line: One proposal holds every refund, and they all happen in one step.
demo.c6.aha: Closing is [one proposal with everyone's refund inside it]. Approve it once and every refund happens in one step, or none do.
demo.c6.before: The Pot has $66.00, and each member put in $150.00. Proposals #0 to #3 are all approved. The last money movement was 30 minutes ago.
demo.c6.b1: The trip is over. The app shows what each person would get back before anyone asks.
demo.c6.b2: Maya signs one request to the Hub.
demo.c6.b3: The Hub reads what's really in the Pot, $66, and splits it by what each person put in: $22 each.
demo.c6.b4: It files one request in the Pot that holds all three refunds. From now on, nobody can add or spend.
demo.c6.b5: Her phone adds her approval. Closing needs extra gas room, so all refunds fit in one step.
demo.c6.b6: Now you're Sam. He sees exactly the three refunds he'd approve.
demo.c6.b7: Sam's approval is the second of two.
demo.c6.b8: The Pot sends all three refunds in a single step. If one failed, none would happen.
demo.c6.b9: The relayer tells the Hub, and the Hub marks Lisbon Trip closed.
demo.c6.b10: Everyone got their share back: $22.00 each.

tour.s1: Maya starts a Pot for the Lisbon trip and keeps the suggested rules: up to $100 without asking, bigger spends go to the group.
tour.s2: Setting it up is free. Maya gets one link to drop in the group chat.
tour.s3: Now you're Leo. Maya's link shows him who's in, what's in the Pot and the rules, before he joins.
tour.s4: He signs in with Google and he's in. Nothing to install, nothing to pay.
tour.s5: Leo chips in $150, like Maya and Sam. The Pot is full: $450 of $450.
tour.s6: You're Maya again. She paid $84 for groceries. Before she asks, the app shows the rules allow it.
tour.s7.checking: Maya asks for her $84 back. Pot checks the rules…
tour.s7: Under $100, so Pot rules approve it on the spot. No one else is asked. Maya gets her $84 back; $366 is left.
tour.s8: Maya wants $300 for the boat tickets. That's over the $100 limit, so she needs one OK from Sam or Leo.
tour.s9: One OK from anyone else is enough. Sam and Leo both get a notification, and either one can give it.
tour.s10: Now you're Leo. He sees exactly what he'd give the OK for: $300 to Maya, for tickets.
tour.s11: Over $100, no one can take money out alone. Leo gave the OK, so the $300 goes to Maya. $66 is left.
tour.s12: You're Maya again. The trip is over, so she asks to close the Pot. Everyone would get $22 back.
tour.s13: Now you're Sam. He checks who gets what back, and approves. Closing needs most of the group.
tour.s14: The Pot is closed and everyone gets their share back: $22 each, in their Pot account. Nobody paid a cent to use Pot.
tour.end.title: That's Pot.
tour.end.l1: A Pot is the group's money, with rules everyone can see.
tour.end.l2: Friends join from a link with Google. Nothing to install.
tour.end.l3: Small spends are approved by the rules. Bigger ones wait for the group's OK.
tour.end.l4: No one can take money out alone. At the end, everyone gets their share back.
tour.end.l5: Free to use: nothing to pay, nothing to set up.
tour.end.note: You'll sign in with Google. For now, Pot runs on demo dollars (test money).

demo.near.p1.summary: Maya's phone signed one request to the Pot Hub, and our relayer paid for it. The Hub created Lisbon Trip as its own Sputnik DAO with no keys: its only seats are the members and the Hub.
demo.near.p2.summary: Joining is a DAO proposal that the Hub approves with its one seat, only if the link's signature checks out. Leo's $150 then passes through the Hub, which writes down who put in what.
demo.near.p3.summary: Nobody voted, yet the DAO paid: the Hub checked the rules, filed proposal #2 and approved it with its rulebot seat, 1 of 1. Then the Pot itself sent Maya $84.
demo.near.p4.summary: Today Leo's OK goes to the Hub, which approves with its rulebot seat. The steps below were recorded before one OK existed: Maya's and Leo's approvals are DAO votes (2 of 3), the path spends over the one-OK limit still take.
demo.near.p5.summary: Closing is one proposal that holds all three refunds, computed from what each person put in. Sam's approval ran them in one step: all of them, or none.
